notes:
Summary of account and current evaluation focus: QuantEdge is a mid-to-large quant trading firm building an inference layer for short-horizon decisioning and risk signals. Primary ask: predictable, low-tail latency for model inference under production burst patterns and an auditable measurement methodology.

Key user requirements (shorthand):
- Workloads: low-latency streaming scoring for tick ingestion (token-by-token/streaming), sub-100ms decision path for short prompts, batch reranking for portfolio signals, embedding/rerank for feature retrieval.
- Targets: want to negotiate SLOs around p50/p95/p99. Rough internal goals shared: p50 <= 8-12ms, p95 <= 40-60ms, p99 <= 120-200ms for the trimmed 128-token streaming scoring path. For non-streaming end-to-end (single-shot 512 tokens) they accept higher tails: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 700ms. These are aggressive and tied to reserved GPU sizing.
- Throughput: typical steady-state ~12k inference requests/minute across 3 regional clusters; burst 3x. Need clear tokens/sec/GPU numbers to plan reserved capacity.

Measurement / SLO alignment items discussed:
- Streaming vs non-streaming: QuantEdge insists on separate SLOs. Streaming SLOs must reflect token-commit latencies (time from server token emission to client receipt) and should be measured client-side. Non-streaming SLOs measured as end-to-end response completion.
- Client-side timing vs server-side timing: major negotiation point. Customer wants "client-observed" p95/p99 for contractual SLA. Redwood proposes canonical server-side spans + an agreed client SDK instrumentation (timestamp at request send -> first byte/last byte). Action: create measurement harness (SDK + server trace mapping) and a one-week mirrored run to align results.
- Sampling and excluded buckets: agree to exclude scheduled maintenance windows and known backfilled retries. Need explicit definition of what counts as "service-side queueing" vs customer slow network.
- Streaming tokenization semantics: define what counts as a token unit for SLO (model tokenizer vs client-side chunking). Must be consistent across RW and QuantEdge test harness.

POC findings (high level):
- Single-GPU baseline (A100-like) for trimmed 128-token streaming path: median ~9ms token latency, p95 ~55ms, p99 ~190ms under synthetic uniform arrival. Observed 2x worse p99 during burst patterns (spikes) when KV-cache warm-up and context length increased to 512 tokens.
- Non-streaming 512-token sample: median 160ms, p95 340ms, p99 680ms. Matches customer's expectation range but tail needs engineering attention.
- Observability gaps: customer-side SDK timestamps not yet integrated into their trading app; TTL for metrics aggregation causes some tail smoothing. Need a real-time ingest of traces for legal auditing.

Operational / SLA negotiation notes:
- Redwood suggested reserved GPU plan: N GPUs per region with a burst pool and automatic fallback to compatible quantized model if tail exceeds agreed threshold. Pricing tied to reserved vs burst hours.
- QuantEdge requests hard language that p95/p99 measured client-side triggers credits if missed for two consecutive business hours. Redwood flagged: need to mature measurement harness to avoid false positives.
- Potential compromise: use dual reporting (server-side canonical + client-side sampled reports). Contract includes a 14-day calibration window with no financial penalties, after which reporting is contractual.

Open technical actions: 
- SE (Amit) to deliver measurement SDK + integration guide by 2026-03-13.
- Run 7-day mirrored measurement (client + server) week of 2026-03-16. Capture streaming token latencies and non-streaming end-to-end times.
- Redwood infra to provide throughput-to-GPU guidance: expected tokens/sec per reserved GPU for QuantEdge models (estimated numbers in drive pricing doc).

Legal / Security items:
- Data residency: EU-specific data feeds must remain in eu-1 region; legal to review data residency clause (SEC-2057).
- Audit trail: require immutable audit logs for model version usage and query hashes for 90 days.

Customer quotes / color: "If the p99 spikes disappear in production we sign the reserved plan — but we need to be able to prove it end-to-end from our app." — Head of ML infra.

Next steps (short):
- Deliver SDK + integration playbook (SE).
- Agree on SLO wording and calibration period in the draft SOW (AE + Legal).
- Complete 7-day mirrored run and produce aligned p50/p95/p99 curves.
- Finalize reserved GPU count and pricing after run.

Attachments: POC raw numbers (drive/quantedge/poc-latency-results-2026-03-05.pdf), pricing draft (drive/pricing/dedicated-reserved-plan-quantedge-2026-03-09.xlsx).
